why: The hall's sky tries to hold the sun at a quarter past noon. A biome can write `visual/sun_angle`, and the overworld's `minecraft:day` timeline overrides it every tick, so the party would see the ordinary sun's course — the line would ship and do nothing. The refusal names what the party would see instead and that moving the sun is world-wide in vanilla (a custom dimension or an edited timeline), never a place's. It declares no unit: the attribute map is bound by `atmosphere/frost-hall`'s twenty admitted lines; what the engine refuses is an id the day cycle overrules, read from the pinned jar's timelines.
